title: Shrimp miR-965 Transfers Tumoricidal Mitochondria
author: Kim, Choi, et al.
materials: Cells were harvested from culture dishes with homogenization buffer (20 mM HEPES–KOH, 220 mM mannitol, and 70 mM sucrose) containing a protease inhibitor mixture (Sigma-Aldrich) and centrifuged at 2300 × g for 5 min. The cell pellet was resuspended with homogenization buffer and incubated on ice for 5 min at 4 °C. Cells were ruptured by 10 strokes using a 27-gauge needle. The homogenate was centrifuged at 5800 × g for 5 min, and mitochondria were harvested. The amount of isolated mitochondria was expressed as protein concentration by using the Bio-Rad protein assay kit (Bio-Rad, Richmond, USA). Mitochondrial transfer was conducted by co-incubating isolated mitochondria with cells (1 × 105 cells/well of a 6-well plate) at 37 °C under 5% CO2 for up to 10 h. For in vivo experiments, mice were administered weekly with 1 × 104 isolated mitochondria per gram of body weight via the tail vein.

steps.title: Culture cells and apply miRNA
steps.instruction: Maintain MDA‑MB‑453 cells (ATCC, RRID: CVCL_0418) in Dulbecco’s MEM (Gibco, catalog 11,885) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco, catalog 16,000,044) at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 95 % O₂ and 5 % CO₂. When confluent, treat the cells for 5 h with either miRNA negative control (MMIR-000-PA-1, System Biosciences), synthetic miR‑965, or the miR‑965 antagomir (Bioneer) using the System Biosciences transfection kit (EXFT10A‑1).

steps.title: Prepare microfluidic device
steps.instruction: Seal cotton‑candy sheets with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) to form a mold, allow the PDMS to harden, then perfuse water through the mold to remove the cotton‑candy fibers, creating channels of approximately 950 nm. Connect each device to polythene tubing (PE10, inner diameter 0.28 mm, Braintree Scientific) and attach an individual peristaltic pump (Dolomite, catalog 3,200,243) for flow control.

steps.title: Transfer mitochondria via microfluidics
steps.instruction: Introduce the isolated mitochondria into the microfluidic device at a flow rate of 10–30 μm/s; after passing through the channels, the mitochondria are delivered into the cultured cells.

steps.title: Isolate mitochondria from cells
steps.instruction: Harvest cells into homogenization buffer (20 mM HEPES‑KOH, 220 mM mannitol, 70 mM sucrose) containing a protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma‑Aldrich). Centrifuge at 2,300 × g for 5 min. Resuspend the pellet in the same buffer, incubate on ice for 5 min at 4 °C, then disrupt cells by passing the suspension ten times through a 27‑gauge needle. Centrifuge the homogenate at 5,800 × g for 5 min and collect the mitochondrial pellet. Determine mitochondrial protein concentration with the Bio‑Rad protein assay kit (Bio‑Rad, Richmond, USA).

steps.title: Co‑incubate mitochondria with target cells
steps.instruction: Add isolated mitochondria to cells seeded at 1 × 10⁵ cells per well of a 6‑well plate and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for up to 10 h. For in‑vivo studies, inject mice weekly via the tail vein with 1 × 10⁴ isolated mitochondria per gram of body weight.

steps.title: Quantify ENDOG mRNA by qRT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Extract RNA and perform TaqMan real‑time PCR using the ENDOG primer/probe set Hs00172770_m1 (Life Technologies) and ACTB housekeeping control Hs03023943_g1 (Life Technologies). Set up reactions with TaqMan Universal PCR Master Mix on an ABI 7000 Real‑Time PCR System (Applied Biosystems). Run the thermal profile: 50 °C for 2 min, 95 °C for 10 min, then 40 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s and 60 °C for 1 min. Calculate relative expression with the 2⁻ΔΔCT method normalized to ACTB. Send extracted miRNA for microarray analysis to Macrogen (South Korea).
